items.english: "Has it come out?" Liu said as if groaning, lifting his swimming head, and out of sheer curiosity, forgetting even his thirst, crawled naked to the side of the jar. At this, Sun Sensei too, shading himself from the sun with his white-feather fan, came hurrying toward the two. When all three together peered into the jar, a thing like a small salamander, flesh-coloured as red clay, was swimming in the wine. In length perhaps three sun. It had a mouth, and it had eyes. As it swam it seemed somehow to be drinking the wine. At the sight of it Liu felt suddenly sick. ...
notes: Kept 'three sun' for length; a sun is about three centimetres. 'Red clay' renders shudei.

items.english: The effect of the barbarian monk's treatment appeared at once. From that day Liu Dacheng abruptly could drink no more wine. Now he will not bear even to smell it, they say. Strangely, from that time Liu's health began to fail little by little. This year is three years since he spat out the wine worm, and no trace remains of the round, fat figure of former years. Skin of poor lustre, greasy still, wraps the harsh bones of his face, and frost-touched hair at the temples lingers only faintly above the temples, and in a year none knows how many times he takes to his bed, they say.
notes: 'hair at the temples' renders sobin; 'above the temples' renders komekami. Kept the hearsay 'they say' for sou de aru.

items.english: Yet it was not Liu's health alone that has failed since then. His estate too has declined headlong, and now of the walled fields counted at three hundred mu, most have passed into other hands. Liu himself, perforce, has taken the plough in unpractised hands and passes his days, day by day, in cheerlessness.
notes: 'walled fields counted at three hundred mu' keeps fukaku no den and mu from the set phrase quoted in p10; mu is a Chinese field measure.
